q: What is the main benefit of a multi-stage build for a TypeScript service?
options: It makes the build run on multiple machines
It automatically produces multi-platform images
It allows multiple CMD instructions
Compilers, devDependencies and sources stay in build stages; the runtime image gets only `dist/` and production `node_modules`
explain: Each `FROM` starts a fresh filesystem. The final stage copies only selected artefacts with `COPY --from`, so TypeScript, `@types/*` and build tools never reach production. Multi-platform is a separate buildx feature.

q: A pod using your image fails with `container has runAsNonRoot and image has non-numeric user (node), cannot verify user is non-root`. What's the fix in the Dockerfile?
options: Use a numeric UID, e.g. `USER 1000:1000`
Remove the `USER` instruction
Add `ENV USER=node`
Switch to `USER root` and drop capabilities
explain: The kubelet can't resolve user names inside the image, so it can only verify `runAsNonRoot` for numeric UIDs. Alternatively set `runAsUser: 1000` in the pod's securityContext — but a numeric `USER` in the image is the robust default.

q: You switch the runtime stage from `node:22-bookworm-slim` to `node:22-alpine` but keep copying `node_modules` from a Debian build stage. The app uses `bcrypt`. What goes wrong and how do you fix it? (select all)
options: Alpine images can't run Node.js at all
Nothing — native modules are platform-independent
`bcrypt`'s native binary was built against glibc and fails to load on musl
Install dependencies in an Alpine-based stage so native modules are built/fetched for musl
explain: Native addons are compiled for a specific libc and CPU architecture. Match the dependency-install stage to the runtime's libc (and architecture). Pure-JS packages are portable; native ones are not.

q: Which is the correct way to use a private npm token during a build?
options: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci` with `docker build --secret id=npmrc,src=$HOME/.npmrc`
`COPY .npmrc .` then `RUN npm ci && rm .npmrc`
`ARG NPM_TOKEN` and write it to `.npmrc` in a `RUN`, deleting it at the end of the same `RUN`
`ENV NPM_TOKEN=...` in the build stage only
explain: Secret mounts exist only during the RUN and never enter layers, history or the cache key. ARG values used by RUN are recorded in history (and in max provenance); a COPY'd file stays in its layer; ENV is stored in the stage config.

q: Your multi-platform CI build takes 25 minutes because `npm ci` and `tsc` run under QEMU for linux/amd64 on an arm64 runner. The app has no native addons. What's the most effective improvement?
options: Build only for arm64
Use `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` for the dependency and compile stages so they run natively, and copy the platform-independent output into each target's runtime stage
Add `--no-cache` to avoid stale layers
Switch the base image to Alpine
explain: JavaScript output and pure-JS dependencies are identical across platforms, so build them once natively (cross-compilation). Only the runtime stage needs the target platform. With native addons, keep the prod-deps stage on the target platform or use native builders.

q: What does `docker buildx imagetools inspect` show for an image built with `--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --sbom=true --provenance=mode=max`?
options: A single manifest for the build machine's platform
Two separate tags, one per platform
An image index with amd64 and arm64 manifests plus attestation manifests with platform `unknown/unknown`
Only the SBOM document
explain: Multi-platform builds produce an index. Attestations (SBOM, provenance) are stored as additional manifests that reference the platform manifest they describe, shown as `unknown/unknown`.

q: Your distroless-based image is permanently `unhealthy`. The Dockerfile has `HEALTHCHECK CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000/healthz || exit 1`. Why?
options: The shell-form health check needs `/bin/sh`, and neither a shell nor curl exists in distroless; use exec form with `/nodejs/bin/node -e "fetch(...)"`
Distroless images don't support health checks
Port 3000 is blocked inside distroless
HEALTHCHECK only works in Kubernetes
explain: Shell-form HEALTHCHECK runs via `/bin/sh -c`, and curl isn't installed either. Use exec form with a binary that exists — Node 22's built-in `fetch` works. `docker inspect -f '{{json .State.Health}}'` shows the failing output.

q: Which statements about `HEALTHCHECK` are true? (select all)
options: Its status is visible in `docker ps` and `docker inspect`
Kubernetes ignores it and uses liveness/readiness/startup probes instead
Plain `docker run` restarts a container automatically when it becomes unhealthy
Compose can use it with `depends_on: condition: service_healthy`
explain: Docker only reports health for standalone containers; it doesn't restart unhealthy ones (Swarm services do replace them). Kubernetes has its own probe mechanism.

q: Which tagging and deployment approach is most robust?
options: Push `latest` on every build and deploy `latest`
Push `sha-<commit>` on every build, add `X.Y.Z`/`X.Y`/`X` on releases, make release tags immutable, and deploy by digest
Re-push `1.0.0` whenever a fix is ready so clients get it automatically
Use the build date as the only tag
explain: SHA tags trace images to commits, semver tags communicate releases, immutability prevents silent overwrites, and digests guarantee the deployed bytes. Rollback is redeploying the previous digest.

q: Why put `ARG GIT_SHA` and the `LABEL org.opencontainers.image.revision=$GIT_SHA` at the end of the Dockerfile rather than the top?
options: A value that changes every commit would invalidate the cache for every later instruction if placed early
Labels must be the last instruction
ARGs at the top are ignored
OCI labels at the top aren't exported to registries
explain: Instructions after a changed build arg (when used) miss the cache. Keeping per-build metadata at the end lets dependency and build layers stay cached.

q: hadolint reports `DL3025` on your Dockerfile. What does it want you to change, and why does it matter?
options: Pin apt package versions, for reproducibility
Use JSON (exec) form for CMD/ENTRYPOINT, so your process receives signals directly and no shell is required
Replace ADD with COPY, to avoid remote downloads
Add a HEALTHCHECK, so orchestrators can monitor the container
explain: Shell form wraps the command in `/bin/sh -c`, which can swallow SIGTERM and breaks in shell-less images. DL3008 is apt pinning and DL3020 is ADD vs COPY.

q: Which practices improve build reproducibility? (select all)
options: `RUN curl -L https://example.com/tool/latest/tool.tgz | tar xz`
`ADD --checksum=sha256:... https://example.com/tool-1.2.3.tgz /tmp/`
`FROM node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:...`
`npm ci` with a committed `package-lock.json`
explain: Digests, lockfiles and checksummed downloads make inputs fixed. Downloading `latest` without verification changes silently between builds.

q: A security reviewer asks: 'If the app is compromised, can the attacker modify the application code inside the container?' Your image copies files as root and runs `USER 1000:1000`. What's the answer?
options: Yes, because the process owns its working directory
It depends on the base image's shell
Yes, because Docker always mounts the image read-write for the container user
No — files are root-owned and not writable by UID 1000; combined with `readOnlyRootFilesystem` in Kubernetes, the filesystem is fully immutable
explain: Ownership matters: `COPY` without `--chown` creates root-owned files that UID 1000 can read but not modify. Only explicitly created writable paths (or volumes, `/tmp`) are writable. `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` adds another layer.
